The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

title.description: Short noun-phrase title for the chapter (under 40 chars). Shown in the table of contents.

summary.description: Optional one-line summary of what this chapter covers. Shown on hover in the table of contents.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__spawn_task
tools.description:
Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

The prompt must stand alone — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation.

The result includes a task_id; call dismiss_task with it if the suggestion later becomes stale.

prompt.description: The initial message for the spawned session. Self-contained — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation. Not shown directly in the UI.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

Show visual content — SVG graphics, diagrams, charts, or interactive HTML widgets — that renders inline alongside your text response.
Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content.
The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.
IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

schema.description:
Show visual content — SVG graphics, diagrams, charts, or interactive HTML widgets — that renders inline alongside your text response.
Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content.
The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.
IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

tools.name: SubagentHandback
tools.description:
Deliver your final report to the agent that spawned you (your caller). Use it once, for that hand-off only: when your work is complete, call SubagentHandback({message: <your full report>}). A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai .../artifact/... link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. <?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## 4bdddc46-3b80-45ec-bc37-523e74d4fda6
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

SKILLS (Prefer the skills shipped with the Figma plugin on the agent being used. If no Figma plugin is installed, use the skills served by the Figma MCP resource):
- /figma-use — MANDATORY before calling use_figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-design — for translating an app page or layout into Figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-design/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-library — for building a design system in Figma from code; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-library/SKILL.md
- /figma-code-connect — for mapping Figma components to codebase components; fallback: skill://figma/figma-code-connect/SKILL.md
- /figma-use-figjam — for FigJam-specific use_f

309	@app.get("/api/projects/{slug}/timeline")
310	def timeline(slug: str):
311	    """EDL resolved into output time, grouped by track, for the timeline view."""
312	    p = inside(PROJECTS, slug)
313	    edl = read_json(p / "edit.json")
314	    if not edl:
315	        return {"duration": 0, "tracks": {}, "warnings": []}
316	    warnings: list[str] = []
317	
318	    def lookup(i):
319	        try:
320	            return A.get(i)
321	        except KeyError:
322	            warnings.append(f"unknown asset {i}")
323	            return None
324	    try:
325	        validate(edl)
326	        spans = build_spans(edl, lookup)
327	    except (EDLError, KeyError, TypeError) as e:
328	        return {"duration": 0, "tracks": {}, "warnings": [f"EDL error: {e}"]}
329	    tracks: dict[str, list] = {"segments": [], "overlays": [], "text": [], "sfx": [], "music": [], "bleeps": [],
330	                               "zooms": []}
331	    t = 0.0
332	    for i, s in enumerate(edl["segments"]):
333	        d = seg_duration(s, lookup)
334	        tracks["segments"].append({"i": i, "start": t, "end": t + d, "type": s.get("type", "source"),
335	                                   "label": s.get("id") or s.get("asset") or f"seg{i}", "src_in": s.get("in"),
336	                                   "src_out": s.get("out"), "speed": s.get("speed", 1), "effects": s.get("effects", []),
337	                                   "mode": s.get("mode") or edl.get("mode", "funny")})
338	        for z in s.get("zoom", []) + [dict(x, shake=True) for x in s.get("shake", [])]:
339	            a = z["at"] if "at" in z else (z["src_at"] - s["in"]) / s.get("speed", 1)
340	            dz = z.get("dur") or (z.get("in", 0.12) + z.get("hold", 0.6) + z.get("out", 0.18))
341	            tracks["zooms"].append({"start": t + a, "end": t + min(a + dz, d),
342	                                    "label": "shake" if z.get("shake") else f"x{z.get('to', 1.3)}"})
343	        t += d
344	    total = t
345	
346	    def add(track, evs, default_dur, label_fn):
347	        for k, ev in enumerate(evs):
348	            at = resolve_time(ev, spans, warnings, f"{track}[{k}]") if ("at" in ev or "src_at" in ev) else 0.0
349	            if at is None:
350	                continue
351	            a = lookup(ev["asset"]) if ev.get("asset") else None
352	            dur = ev.get("dur") or (ev.get("until", total) - at if track == "music" else None) \
353	                or (a.get("tail_s") or a.get("duration_s") if a else None) or default_dur
354	            tracks[track].append({"k": k, "start": at, "end": min(total, at + dur), "label": label_fn(ev, a),
355	                                  "asset": ev.get("asset"), "thumb": a.get("thumb") if a else None})
356	    add("overlays", edl.get("overlays", []), 1.5, lambda e, a: f"{e['type']}: {(a or {}).get('title') or e.get('file')}")
357	    add("text", edl.get("text", []), 1.2, lambda e, a: e.get("text", ""))
358	    add("sfx", edl.get("audio", {}).get("sfx", []), 1.0, lambda e, a: (a or {}).get("title") or e.get("asset"))
359	    add("music", edl.get("audio", {}).get("music", []), total, lambda e, a: (a or {}).get("title") or e.get("asset"))
360	    add("bleeps", edl.get("audio", {}).get("bleeps", []), 0.4, lambda e, a: "bleep")
361	    return {"duration": total, "tracks": tracks, "warnings": warnings, "format": edl.get("format", "landscape")}

385	class Job:
386	    def __init__(self, slug: str, stage: str, cmd: list[str], cwd: Path):
387	        self.id = uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]
388	        self.slug, self.stage, self.cmd, self.cwd = slug, stage, cmd, cwd
389	        self.status = "running"
390	        self.lines: list[str] = []
391	        self.started = time.time()
392	        self.ended: float | None = None
393	        self.rc: int | None = None
394	        self.proc: subprocess.Popen | None = None
395	        self.result: dict | None = None     # set from a "@@RESULT {json}" line printed by the command
396	        threading.Thread(target=self._run, daemon=True).start()
397	
398	    def _run(self):
399	        env = dict(os.environ, PYTHONUNBUFFERED="1", PYTHONIOENCODING="utf-8")
400	        try:
401	            self.proc = subprocess.Popen(self.cmd, cwd=self.cwd, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
402	                                         text=True, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace", env=env)
403	            for line in self.proc.stdout:
404	                if line.startswith("@@RESULT "):
405	                    try:
406	                        self.result = json.loads(line[9:])
407	                    except ValueError:
408	                        pass
409	                    continue
410	                self.lines.append(line.rstrip())
411	                if len(self.lines) > 4000:
412	                    del self.lines[:1000]
413	            self.rc = self.proc.wait()
414	            self.status = "done" if self.rc == 0 else "failed"
415	        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
416	            self.lines.append(f"!! {e}")
417	            self.status = "failed"
418	        self.ended = time.time()
419	
420	    def public(self, tail: int = 200) -> dict:
421	        return {"id": self.id, "slug": self.slug, "stage": self.stage, "status": self.status, "rc": self.rc,
422	                "started": self.started, "elapsed": round((self.ended or time.time()) - self.started, 1),
423	                "log": self.lines[-tail:], "result": self.result}

        parts = dict(a["parts"])
        for k, v in b["parts"].items():
            parts[k] = parts.get(k, 0) + v
        th = max(parts, key=parts.get) if parts else (a["theme"] or b["theme"])
        return {"theme": th, "start": a["start"], "end": b["end"], "parts": parts}
    # repeatedly merge the shortest sub-10 s run into its shorter neighbour (the intro keeps its own label)
    while len(runs) > 1:

input.message:
The publishing workflow is built, and the `auto-dig` episode plus its 3 shorts now have generated publish.json files. I checked the backend with a FastAPI TestClient and `node --check ui/app.js` passes. I haven't seen the UI in a browser: the live server on 8765 still returns 404 for `/api/pipeline`. **Please restart the UI server (`uv run mcs ui`)** to load the new routes.

Two things to know first:
- **No `claude` CLI on PATH here.** Everything below came from the built-in rule-based writer. If `claude` is on PATH later, generation asks it for the creative parts (90s timeout) and falls back to the built-in writer if that fails.
- **`out/auto-dig.mp4` can't be opened right now** ("moov atom not found"). It's probably being re-rendered by the other session. The board's poster frame for auto-dig stays empty until that file is complete; nothing breaks meanwhile.

## Files
- **New:** `C:\Users\edmem\OneDrive\Desktop\Minecraft Channel\studio\mcstudio\publish.py` (data model, status rules, writer, chapters, credits, image prompts, poster frames). Command line: `python -m mcstudio.publish generate <slug> [--no-llm]` prints `@@RESULT {json}`; `... show <slug>` prints the data.
- **`mcstudio/server.py`:** one new section just above `app.mount(...)`.
- **`ui/app.js`:** new section before `boot();`. Three one-line edits to existing code: `pipeline: Pipeline` in the `route()` table, a `["publish","Publish"]` tab and `publish: PublishTab` in `Project()`.
- **`ui/index.html`:** a "Publishing" nav item after Episodes.
- **`ui/style.css`:** new section at the end.
- **Generated:** `projects/auto-dig/publish.json`. Each regenerate backs up the previous file to `projects/auto-dig/history/publish.<timestamp>.json`.
- I did not touch `autoplan.py`, `demos.py` or any edit.json.

## Endpoints
- `GET /api/pipeline`: all episodes (shorts grouped under their parent) with status, title, duration, poster image, scheduled date, URL and a shorts summary.
- `GET /api/projects/{slug}/publish`: the publish data plus status labels, video path, thumbnail, tag character count, checklist and any running job. A short's slug returns its parent's data.
- `PATCH /api/projects/{slug}/publish`: any fields. Tags and hashtags can be a list or a comma string. Calling it with a short's slug updates that short's entry inside the parent's file.
- `POST /api/projects/{slug}/publish/generate`: runs generation as a Job (stage `publish`).
- Extras I added:
  - `POST .../publish/thumbnail` saves an uploaded image as `projects/<slug>/thumbnail.<ext>`.
  - `POST .../publish/open-folder` opens Explorer with the final video selected.

## How status works
Order: `editing` → `rendered` (shown as "Awaiting upload") → `uploaded` → `scheduled` → `published`, plus `archived`.
- **Default when there's no publish.json:** `rendered` if `out/<slug>.mp4` exists, otherwise `editing`.
- **Archived by default:** I made demo projects and `_`-prefixed folders start as `archived` so they don't clutter the board. That was my call; say if you want them visible.
- **Automatic moves when read:** a stored `editing` shows as `rendered` once the final render exists, and `scheduled` shows as `published` once its date has passed.
- **On PATCH:**
  - An unknown status is rejected (400).
  - Moving to `scheduled` without a date is rejected (400).
  - Setting `scheduled_at` sets the status to scheduled if the date is in the future, or to published if it's in the past and there's a YouTube URL.
  - Adding a URL to an episode in editing/awaiting upload moves it to published (or to scheduled if the date is still ahead).
  - `uploaded_at` is filled in automatically.
- **Changing the thumbnail text** also rewrites the quoted text inside both prompts that contain it.
- **Regenerating** keeps status, schedule, uploaded date, URL and notes.

## UI
- **Publishing board (#/pipeline):** columns Editing · Awaiting upload · Uploaded · Scheduled · Published, with an "show archived" toggle.
  - Cards show poster, duration, a shorts badge with how many are up, "copy ready", the scheduled date and a YouTube link.
  - Cards move with ← → or drag-and-drop. Moving to Scheduled without a date opens the Publish tab and asks for one. Clicking a card opens the episode's Publish tab.
- **Publish tab on the episode page:**
  - Status dropdown, date-and-time picker for the schedule, YouTube URL.
  - "✨ Generate" (watches the job), "Copy all", and a checklist: video, title, description, tags, thumbnail image, scheduled.
  - Title options you click to use; thumbnail text options as chips.
  - Fields: Title, Description, Tags (counter against 500), Hashtags, Thumbnail text, Thumbnail prompt with text, Thumbnail prompt without text, Shorts cover prompt. Each has its own Copy button (with a fallback when the clipboard API is blocked) and saves automatically about 650ms after you stop typing.
  - Side panel: video player, path, Open folder / Download / Copy path, thumbnail upload with ChatGPT steps, chapters, notes, and licence warnings.
  - Shorts section: each short has its own video, status, schedule, copyable title/description/tags/9:16 cover prompt and "Copy all". On a short's own page the tab says its copy lives with the episode and highlights it.

## Generated auto-dig content
**Title options (first one is the title):**
1. I Tried to Dig to Bedrock… It Went Horribly Wrong
2. I Tried to Dig to Bedrock (and Instantly Regretted It)
3. Digging Straight Down in Minecraft Was a Mistake
4. I Can't Even Craft a Pickaxe… (Dig to Bedrock)
5. The Dig to Bedrock Challenge Went Wrong

```
I Tried to Dig to Bedrock in Minecraft… and it did NOT go to plan.

The challenge: dig straight down, all the way to bedrock. First problem: crafting a pickaxe, which turned into a full sticks-and-planks lecture that went off the rails. Then I finally started digging straight down, and it went horribly wrong, fast. (Turns out you can't breathe underwater.)

⏱ Chapters
0:00 The Challenge
0:20 Crafting a Pickaxe (Badly)
1:19 Digging Down… Big Mistake

🦎 New here? Subscribe to @Crodie for more Minecraft, but it goes wrong! Drop a comment with what I should try next 👇

#minecraft #minecraftfunny #minecraftchallenge
```
- Chapter times are in final-video time, computed from the edit's segments.
- There's no music credit because the only music, `music.2` "Unidentified Funny Track 02", has an unknown licence. The generator flags it as a possible Content ID claim and suggests swapping it for a credited track. Kevin MacLeod tracks get the standard CC-BY credit, and `CREDITS.txt` is added if present.

**Tags (23, 465 of 500 characters):** minecraft, crodie, minecraft funny, minecraft funny moments, minecraft challenge, minecraft gameplay, minecraft survival, minecraft crafting, how to craft a pickaxe, minecraft pickaxe, minecraft dig to bedrock, digging straight down, minecraft mining, minecraft caving, minecraft scary moments, minecraft death, minecraft fails, minecraft funny death, minecraft drowning, minecraft water, funny minecraft video, minecraft memes, crodie minecraft

**Thumbnail text:** TOO DEEP! (other options: BIG MISTAKE, NOT AGAIN, HOW?!)

```
Attach: Crodie/profile pic.png and Crodie/mc skin.png as reference (optional pose refs: studio/brand/crodie/characters/char_head_shocked.png, char_mining_pickaxe.png). Keep Crodie exactly on-model: same colours, proportions and face.

Create a 16:9 YouTube thumbnail (1280x720) for a Minecraft video called "I Tried to Dig to Bedrock… It Went Horribly Wrong".

CHARACTER (Crodie large and dead-centre, about 60% of the frame height, the clear hero of the image): Crodie, the channel mascot: a cute, chunky, blocky Minecraft-style lizard/gecko built from voxel cubes. Lime-green (#92AE22) and leaf-green (#437420) pixel-block skin with scattered orange (#EF7718) spots, a cream (#FCDFB5) belly and lower jaw, big glossy amber-brown eyes with bright white highlights, a wide expressive mouth (normally a big open smile), and a long curled striped tail. ## Files
```
- **New:** `C:\Users\edmem\OneDrive\Desktop\Minecraft Channel\studio\mcstudio\publish.py` (data model, status rules, writer, chapters, credits, image prompts, poster frames). Command line: `python -m mcstudio.publish generate <slug> [--no-llm]` prints `@@RESULT {json}`; `... show <slug>` prints the data.
- **`mcstudio/server.py`:** one new section just above `app.mount(...)`.

## Endpoints
- `GET /api/pipeline`: all episodes (shorts grouped under their parent) with status, title, duration, poster image, scheduled date, URL and a shorts summary.
- `GET /api/projects/{slug}/publish`: the publish data plus status labels, video path, thumbnail, tag character count, checklist and any running job. A short's slug returns its parent's data.
- `PATCH /api/projects/{slug}/publish`: any fields. Tags and hashtags can be a list or a comma string. Calling it with a short's slug updates that short's entry inside the parent's file.
- `POST /api/projects/{slug}/publish/generate`: runs generation as a Job (stage `publish`).
- Extras I added:
  - `POST .../publish/thumbnail` saves an uploaded image as `projects/<slug>/thumbnail.<ext>`.
  - `POST .../publish/open-folder` opens Explorer with the final video selected.

## How status works
Order: `editing` → `rendered` (shown as "Awaiting upload") → `uploaded` → `scheduled` → `published`, plus `archived`.
- **Default when there's no publish.json:** `rendered` if `out/<slug>.mp4` exists, otherwise `editing`.
- **Archived by default:** I made demo projects and `_`-prefixed folders start as `archived` so they don't clutter the board. That was my call; say if you want them visible.
- **Automatic moves when read:** a stored `editing` shows as `rendered` once the final render exists, and `scheduled` shows as `published` once its date has passed.
- **On PATCH:**
  - An unknown status is rejected (400).
  - Moving to `scheduled` without a date is rejected (400).
  - Setting `scheduled_at` sets the status to scheduled if the date is in the future, or to published if it's in the past and there's a YouTube URL.
  - Adding a URL to an episode in editing/awaiting upload moves it to published (or to scheduled if the date is still ahead).
  - `uploaded_at` is filled in automatically.
- **Changing the thumbnail text** also rewrites the quoted text inside both prompts that contain it.
- **Regenerating** keeps status, schedule, uploaded date, URL and notes.

## UI
- **Publishing board (#/pipeline):** columns Editing · Awaiting upload · Uploaded · Scheduled · Published, with an "show archived" toggle.
  - Cards show poster, duration, a shorts badge with how many are up, "copy ready", the scheduled date and a YouTube link.
  - Cards move with ← → or drag-and-drop. Moving to Scheduled without a date opens the Publish tab and asks for one. Clicking a card opens the episode's Publish tab.
- **Publish tab on the episode page:**
  - Status dropdown, date-and-time picker for the schedule, YouTube URL.
  - "✨ Generate" (watches the job), "Copy all", and a checklist: video, title, description, tags, thumbnail image, scheduled.
  - Title options you click to use; thumbnail text options as chips.
  - Fields: Title, Description, Tags (counter against 500), Hashtags, Thumbnail text, Thumbnail prompt with text, Thumbnail prompt without text, Shorts cover prompt. Each has its own Copy button (with a fallback when the clipboard API is blocked) and saves automatically about 650ms after you stop typing.
  - Side panel: video player, path, Open folder / Download / Copy path, thumbnail upload with ChatGPT steps, chapters, notes, and licence warnings.
